220	class _Parser:
221	    def __init__(self, source: str) -> None:
222	        self.lexer = _Lexer(source)
223	        self.current = self.lexer.next_token()
224	
225	    # -- token stream ------------------------------------------------------
226	
227	    def peek(self) -> _Token:
228	        return self.current
229	
230	    def advance(self) -> _Token:
231	        tok = self.current
232	        if tok.kind != "eof":
233	            self.current = self.lexer.next_token()
234	        return tok
235	
236	    def raise_error(self, code: str, message: str, tok: _Token | None = None) -> None:
237	        tok = tok if tok is not None else self.peek()
238	        raise RTLParseError(code, message, tok.line, tok.column)
239	
240	    def at_punct(self, text: str) -> bool:
241	        tok = self.peek()
242	        return tok.kind == "punct" and tok.text == text
243	
244	    def at_ident(self, text: str) -> bool:
245	        tok = self.peek()
246	        return tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text == text
247	
248	    def expect_punct(self, text: str) -> _Token:
249	        tok = self.peek()
250	        if tok.kind != "punct" or tok.text != text:
251	            self.raise_error("syntax_error", f"expected {text!r} but found {_describe(tok)}")
252	        return self.advance()
253	
254	    def expect_name(self, what: str) -> _Token:
255	        tok = self.peek()
256	        if tok.kind != "ident" or tok.text in _SUPPORTED_HEADER or tok.text in _UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORDS:
257	            self.raise_error("syntax_error", f"expected {what} but found {_describe(tok)}")
258	        return self.advance()
259	
260	    # -- top level ---------------------------------------------------------
261	
262	    def parse_source(self) -> dict:
263	        modules = []
264	        names: set[str] = set()
265	        while self.peek().kind != "eof":
266	            modules.append(self.parse_module(names))
267	        if not modules:
268	            self.raise_error("syntax_error", "source contains no module")
269	        return {"modules": modules}
270	
271	    def parse_module(self, names: set[str]) -> dict:
272	        if not self.at_ident("module"):
273	            self.raise_error(
274	                "syntax_error",
275	                f"expected 'module' but found {_describe(self.peek())}",
276	            )
277	        self.advance()
278	        name_tok = self.expect_name("module name")
279	        if name_tok.text in names:
280	            self.raise_error("duplicate_name", f"duplicate module name {name_tok.text!r}", name_tok)
281	        names.add(name_tok.text)
282	        if self.at_punct("#"):
283	            self.raise_error(
284	                "unsupported_construct",
285	                "parameterized module headers are not supported",
286	            )
287	        self.expect_punct("(")
288	
289	        ports: list[dict] = []
290	        declared: set[str] = set()
291	        if not self.at_punct(")"):
292	            self.parse_port_list(ports, declared)
293	        self.expect_punct(")")
294	        self.expect_punct(";")
295	
296	        nets: list[dict] = []
297	        assigns: list[dict] = []
298	        refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]] = []
299	        while not self.at_ident("endmodule"):
300	            tok = self.peek()
301	            if tok.kind == "eof":
302	                self.raise_error("syntax_error", "unexpected end of input inside module")
303	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text == "wire":
304	                self.advance()
305	                self.parse_net_decl(nets, declared)
306	            elif tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text == "assign":
307	                self.advance()
308	                assigns.append(self.parse_assign(refs))
309	            elif tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text in _UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORDS:
310	                self.raise_error(
311	                    "unsupported_construct",
312	                    f"construct {tok.text!r} is not supported",
313	                )
314	            elif tok.kind == "ident":
315	                self.raise_error(
316	                    "unsupported_construct",
317	                    f"module item starting with {tok.text!r} is not supported "
318	                    "(instances and procedural blocks are outside the subset)",
319	                )
320	            elif tok.kind == "punct" and tok.text == "#":
321	                self.raise_error("unsupported_construct", "parameter syntax is not supported")
322	            else:
323	                self.raise_error("syntax_error", f"unexpected {_describe(tok)} inside module")
324	        self.advance()  # consume endmodule
325	
326	        # Declarations span the whole module body, so forward references are
327	        # legal; resolve every referenced name after the body is parsed.
328	        for ref_name, ref_tok in refs:
329	            if ref_name not in declared:
330	                self.raise_error(
331	                    "undeclared_signal",
332	                    f"signal {ref_name!r} is not declared in this module",
333	                    ref_tok,
334	                )
335	
336	        return {"name": name_tok.text, "ports": ports, "nets": nets, "assigns": assigns}
337	
338	    # -- declarations ------------------------------------------------------
339	
340	    def add_declared(self, declared: set[str], name_tok: _Token) -> None:
341	        if name_tok.text in declared:
342	            self.raise_error(
343	                "duplicate_name",
344	                f"duplicate port/net name {name_tok.text!r}",
345	                name_tok,
346	            )
347	        declared.add(name_tok.text)
348	
349	    def parse_port_list(self, ports: list[dict], declared: set[str]) -> None:
350	        while True:
351	            tok = self.peek()
352	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.text in _DIRECTIONS:
353	                direction = tok.text
354	                self.advance()
355	            elif tok.kind == "ident":
356	                # A bare name in the header is the non-ANSI style.
357	                self.raise_error(
358	                    "unsupported_construct",
359	                    "non-ANSI port declarations are not supported",
360	                )
361	            else:
362	                self.raise_error(
363	                    "syntax_error",
364	                    f"expected port direction but found {_describe(tok)}",
365	                )
366	            # ANSI headers may say ``input wire [..] a``; wire is the only
367	            # net kind in the subset, anything else (reg, signed, ...) is
368	            # rejected as unsupported.
369	            if self.at_ident("wire"):
370	                self.advance()
371	            elif self.peek().kind == "ident" and self.peek().text in _UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORDS:
372	                self.raise_error(
373	                    "unsupported_construct",
374	                    f"port kind {self.peek().text!r} is not supported",
375	                )
376	            width = self.parse_optional_range()
377	            while True:
378	                if self.peek().kind == "ident" and self.peek().text in _UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORDS:
379	                    self.raise_error(
380	                        "unsupported_construct",
381	                        f"port kind {self.peek().text!r} is not supported",
382	                    )
383	                name_tok = self.expect_name("port name")
384	                self.add_declared(declared, name_tok)
385	                ports.append({"name": name_tok.text, "direction": direction, "width": width})
386	                if not self.at_punct(","):
387	                    return
388	                self.advance()
389	                if any(self.at_ident(d) for d in _DIRECTIONS):
390	                    break  # next direction group
391	
392	    def parse_net_decl(self, nets: list[dict], declared: set[str]) -> None:
393	        width = self.parse_optional_range()
394	        while True:
395	            name_tok = self.expect_name("net name")
396	            self.add_declared(declared, name_tok)
397	            nets.append({"name": name_tok.text, "width": width})
398	            if not self.at_punct(","):
399	                break
400	            self.advance()
401	        self.expect_punct(";")
402	
403	    def parse_optional_range(self) -> int:
404	        if not self.at_punct("["):
405	            return 1
406	        self.advance()
407	        msb = self.parse_range_endpoint()
408	        self.expect_punct(":")
409	        lsb = self.parse_range_endpoint()
410	        self.expect_punct("]")
411	        return abs(msb - lsb) + 1
412	
413	    def parse_range_endpoint(self) -> int:
414	        tok = self.peek()
415	        if tok.kind != "number" or tok.number[1] is not None:
416	            self.raise_error(
417	                "invalid_range",
418	                "range endpoint must be a non-negative decimal constant",
419	            )
420	        self.advance()
421	        return tok.number[0]
422	
423	    # -- statements --------------------------------------------------------
424	
425	    def parse_assign(self, refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]]) -> dict:
426	        target = self.parse_expr(refs)
427	        self.expect_punct("=")
428	        value = self.parse_expr(refs)
429	        self.expect_punct(";")
430	        return {"target": target, "value": value}
431	
432	    # -- expressions -------------------------------------------------------
433	
434	    def parse_expr(self, refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]], min_prec: int = 1) -> dict:
435	        left = self.parse_unary(refs)
436	        while True:
437	            tok = self.peek()
438	            if tok.kind != "punct":
439	                break
440	            prec = _BINARY_PREC.get(tok.text)
441	            if prec is None or prec < min_prec:
442	                break
443	            self.advance()
444	            next_min = prec if tok.text in _RIGHT_ASSOC else prec + 1
445	            right = self.parse_expr(refs, next_min)
446	            left = {"kind": "binary", "op": tok.text, "left": left, "right": right}
447	        return left
448	
449	    def parse_unary(self, refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]]) -> dict:
450	        tok = self.peek()
451	        if tok.kind == "punct" and tok.text in _UNARY_OPS:
452	            self.advance()
453	            operand = self.parse_unary(refs)
454	            return {"kind": "unary", "op": tok.text, "operand": operand}
455	        return self.parse_postfix(refs)
456	
457	    def parse_postfix(self, refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]]) -> dict:
458	        node = self.parse_primary(refs)
459	        while self.at_punct("["):
460	            bracket = self.advance()
461	            first = self.parse_expr(refs)
462	            if self.at_punct(":"):
463	                self.advance()
464	                second = self.parse_expr(refs)
465	                self.expect_punct("]")
466	                msb = self.require_const_endpoint(first, bracket)
467	                lsb = self.require_const_endpoint(second, bracket)
468	                node = {"kind": "range_select", "base": node, "msb": msb, "lsb": lsb}
469	            else:
470	                self.expect_punct("]")
471	                node = {"kind": "bit_select", "base": node, "index": first}
472	        return node
473	
474	    def require_const_endpoint(self, node: dict, at: _Token) -> int:
475	        if node.get("kind") != "const" or node["width"] is not None or node["value"] < 0:
476	            self.raise_error(
477	                "invalid_range",
478	                "range select endpoints must be non-negative decimal constants",
479	                at,
480	            )
481	        return node["value"]
482	
483	    def parse_primary(self, refs: list[tuple[str, _Token]]) -> dict:
484	        tok = self.peek()
485	        if tok.kind == "number":
486	            self.advance()
487	            value, width = tok.number
488	            return {"kind": "const", "value": value, "width": width}
489	        if tok.kind == "ident":
490	            if tok.text in _SUPPORTED_HEADER or tok.text in _UNSUPPORTED_KEYWORDS:
491	                self.raise_error("syntax_error", f"unexpected keyword {tok.text!r} in expression")
492	            self.advance()
493	            refs.append((tok.text, tok))
494	            return {"kind": "ref", "name": tok.text}
495	        if tok.kind == "punct" and tok.text == "(":
496	            self.advance()
497	            node = self.parse_expr(refs)
498	            self.expect_punct(")")
499	            return node
500	        if tok.kind == "punct" and tok.text == "{":
501	            self.advance()
502	            items = [self.parse_expr(refs)]
503	            while self.at_punct(","):
504	                self.advance()
505	                items.append(self.parse_expr(refs))
506	            self.expect_punct("}")
507	            return {"kind": "concat", "items": items}
508	        self.raise_error("syntax_error", f"expected expression but found {_describe(tok)}")

511	def parse(source: str) -> dict:
512	    """Parse one Verilog source text into a JSON-serializable circuit IR."""

import json
import unittest

from siliconrail import RTLParseError
from siliconrail.service import Service

from test_http import HttpTestBase


def analyze(source):
    return Service().analyze_widths(source)


class AnalyzeWidthsDirectTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_ref_and_sized_const_use_declared_width(self):
        ir = analyze(
            "module m(input [7:0] a, output [7:0] o);\n"
            "assign o = a + 4'b1010;\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        assign = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]
        value = assign["value"]
        self.assertEqual(value["kind"], "binary")
        self.assertEqual(value["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(value["left"], {"kind": "ref", "name": "a", "width": 8})
        self.assertEqual(value["right"]["width"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(assign["target"]["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(
            (assign["target_width"], assign["value_width"], assign["conversion"]),
            (8, 8, "exact"),
        )

    def test_unsized_decimal_constants(self):
        ir = analyze(
            "module m(output [63:0] a, output [63:0] b, output [63:0] c);\n"
            "assign a = 0;\n"
            "assign b = 42;\n"
            "assign c = 4294967296;\n"  # 2**32
            "endmodule"
        )
        assigns = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"]
        self.assertEqual(assigns[0]["value"]["width"], 32)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[1]["value"]["width"], 32)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[2]["value"]["width"], 33)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[2]["conversion"], "zero_extend")

    def test_selects_and_concat(self):
        ir = analyze(
            "module m(input [15:0] a, output [7:0] o);\n"
            "wire [3:0] w;\n"
            "assign w = a[9:6];\n"
            "assign o = {a[3], a[11:8], 3'b101};\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        assigns = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"]
        self.assertEqual(assigns[0]["value"]["width"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[0]["conversion"], "exact")
        concat = assigns[1]["value"]
        self.assertEqual(concat["kind"], "concat")
        self.assertEqual(concat["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual([item["width"] for item in concat["items"]], [1, 4, 3])

    def test_operator_width_rules(self):
        ir = analyze(
            "module m(input [7:0] a, input [3:0] b, output [15:0] o);\n"
            "wire [7:0] w;\n"
            "assign w = a & b;\n"          # max(8, 4)
            "assign w = a << b;\n"         # left width
            "assign w = -a;\n"             # operand width
            "assign w = ~a;\n"
            "assign o[0] = !a;\n"
            "assign o[1] = &a;\n"
            "assign o[2] = a == b;\n"
            "assign o[3] = a && b;\n"
            "assign o[4] = a < b;\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        assigns = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"]
        self.assertEqual(assigns[0]["value"]["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[1]["value"]["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[2]["value"]["width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(assigns[3]["value"]["width"], 8)
        for assign in assigns[4:]:
            self.assertEqual(assign["value"]["width"], 1)
            self.assertEqual(assign["conversion"], "exact")

    def test_conversion_labels(self):
        ir = analyze(
            "module m(input [7:0] a, output [3:0] s, output [15:0] big, output [7:0] same);\n"
            "assign s = a;\n"
            "assign big = a;\n"
            "assign same = a;\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        assigns = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"]
        self.assertEqual(assigns[0]["conversion"], "truncate")
        self.assertEqual(assigns[1]["conversion"], "zero_extend")
        self.assertEqual(assigns[2]["conversion"], "exact")

    def test_truncation_does_not_rewrite_constants(self):
        ir = analyze("module m(output [3:0] o); assign o = 8'hFF; endmodule")
        assign = ir["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]
        self.assertEqual(assign["conversion"], "truncate")
        self.assertEqual(assign["value"]["value"], 0xFF)
        self.assertEqual(assign["value"]["width"], 8)

    def test_parse_result_unchanged_and_source_order_preserved(self):
        source = (
            "module m(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, output [8:0] o);\n"
            "wire [8:0] s;\n"
            "assign s = a + b;\n"
            "assign o = s;\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        service = Service()
        parsed = service.parse_rtl(source)
        analyzed = service.analyze_widths(source)
        # parse_rtl output is untouched by the width pass
        self.assertEqual(service.parse_rtl(source), parsed)
        self.assertNotIn("width", parsed["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]["target"])
        # same skeleton, in source order, with annotations added
        self.assertEqual([a["target"]["name"] for a in analyzed["modules"][0]["assigns"]], ["s", "o"])
        self.assertEqual(analyzed["modules"][0]["nets"], [{"name": "s", "width": 9}])
        # max(8, 8) for the add, then zero-extended onto the 9-bit net
        self.assertEqual(analyzed["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]["value_width"], 8)
        self.assertEqual(analyzed["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]["conversion"], "zero_extend")

    def test_json_serializable_and_deterministic(self):
        source = (
            "module m(input [3:0] a, output [7:0] o);\n"
            "assign o = {a, a[1:0], 2'b10} << 1;\n"
            "endmodule"
        )
        first = json.dumps(analyze(source), sort_keys=True)
        second = json.dumps(analyze(source), sort_keys=True)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_non_string_raises_type_error(self):
        for bad in (None, 42, b"module m; endmodule", ["x"]):
            with self.subTest(bad=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    Service().analyze_widths(bad)

    def test_parse_failures_match_parse_rtl(self):
        service = Service()
        sources = [
            "",
            "module m(input a, output o); assign o = ghost; endmodule",
            "module m(output o); assign o = 1; assign o = 2; endmodule\nmodule m; endmodule",
            "module m(output o); wire [3:0] w; assign o = w; always @* begin end endmodule",
            "module m(output o); assign o = 1'bx; endmodule",
        ]
        for source in sources:
            with self.subTest(source=source):
                with self.assertRaises(RTLParseError) as direct:
                    service.analyze_widths(source)
                with self.assertRaises(RTLParseError) as baseline:
                    service.parse_rtl(source)
                for exc in (direct.exception, baseline.exception):
                    self.assertTrue(exc.message)
                self.assertEqual(
                    (direct.exception.code, direct.exception.line, direct.exception.column),
                    (baseline.exception.code, baseline.exception.line, baseline.exception.column),
                )


class AnalyzeWidthsHttpTest(HttpTestBase):
    def post_widths(self, body):
        raw = body if isinstance(body, (bytes, str)) else json.dumps(body)
        return self.request("POST", "/v1/rtl/widths", body=raw,
                            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})

    def test_success_matches_direct_entry(self):
        source = "module m(input [3:0] a, output [7:0] o); assign o = a; endmodule"
        status, payload = self.post_widths({"source": source})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload, Service().analyze_widths(source))
        assign = payload["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]
        self.assertEqual(assign["conversion"], "zero_extend")

    def test_parse_error_maps_to_422_with_four_fields(self):
        status, payload = self.post_widths({"source": "module m(output o); assign o = nope; endmodule"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 422)
        self.assertEqual(set(payload["error"]), {"code", "line", "column", "message"})
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "undeclared_signal")

    def test_invalid_requests_map_to_400(self):
        for body in (json.dumps([1]), json.dumps({}), json.dumps({"source": 7}), "{not json"):
            with self.subTest(body=body):
                status, payload = self.post_widths(body)
                self.assertEqual(status, 400)
                self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "invalid_request")

    def test_extra_fields_are_allowed(self):
        source = "module m(input a, output o); assign o = a; endmodule"
        status, payload = self.post_widths({"source": source, "extra": 1})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]["conversion"], "exact")

    def test_parse_endpoint_still_unannotated(self):
        source = "module m(input a, output o); assign o = a; endmodule"
        status, payload = self.post({"source": source})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertNotIn("width", payload["modules"][0]["assigns"][0]["target"])
        self.assertNotIn("conversion", payload["modules"][0]["assigns"][0])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import json
import threading
import unittest
from http.client import HTTPConnection
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer

from siliconrail.server import Handler


class HttpTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        cls.port = cls.server.server_address[1]
        cls.thread = threading.Thread(target=cls.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        cls.thread.start()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.server.shutdown()
        cls.server.server_close()
        cls.thread.join()

    def request(self, method, path, body=None, headers=None):
        conn = HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.port, timeout=5)
        conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers or {})
        resp = conn.getresponse()
        raw = resp.read()
        conn.close()
        return resp.status, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))

    def post(self, body, content_type="application/json"):
        raw = body if isinstance(body, (bytes, str)) else json.dumps(body)
        return self.request("POST", "/v1/rtl/parse", body=raw, headers={"Content-Type": content_type})


class RtlParseEndpointTest(HttpTestBase):
    def test_success_matches_direct_entry(self):
        source = "module m(input a, output o); assign o = ~a; endmodule"
        status, payload = self.post({"source": source})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        from siliconrail.service import Service

        self.assertEqual(payload, Service().parse_rtl(source))

    def test_parse_error_maps_to_422_with_four_fields(self):
        status, payload = self.post({"source": "module m(input a, output o);\nassign o = nope;\nendmodule"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 422)
        error = payload["error"]
        self.assertEqual(set(error), {"code", "line", "column", "message"})
        self.assertEqual(error["code"], "undeclared_signal")
        self.assertEqual(error["line"], 2)
        self.assertIsInstance(error["column"], int)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(error["column"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(error["message"])
        self.assertNotIn("modules", payload)

    def test_parse_error_is_stable_across_calls(self):
        source = "module m(output o); assign o = ghost; endmodule"
        status1, first = self.post({"source": source})
        status2, second = self.post({"source": source})
        self.assertEqual((status1, status2), (422, 422))
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_invalid_requests_map_to_400(self):
        bad_bodies = [
            json.dumps([1, 2]),
            json.dumps("module m; endmodule"),
            json.dumps(42),
            json.dumps({}),
            json.dumps({"source": 42}),
            json.dumps({"source": None}),
            "{not json",
            "module m; endmodule",
        ]
        for body in bad_bodies:
            with self.subTest(body=body):
                status, payload = self.post(body)
                self.assertEqual(status, 400)
                self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "invalid_request")
                self.assertTrue(payload["error"]["message"])

    def test_invalid_utf8_is_invalid_request(self):
        status, payload = self.post(b'{"source": "module \xff"}')
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "invalid_request")

    def test_empty_source_maps_to_422_syntax_error(self):
        status, payload = self.post({"source": ""})
        self.assertEqual(status, 422)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "syntax_error")

    def test_extra_fields_are_allowed(self):
        source = "module m(input a, output o); assign o = a; endmodule"
        status, payload = self.post({"source": source, "extra": [1, 2]})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["modules"][0]["name"], "m")

    def test_unknown_post_path_is_404(self):
        status, payload = self.request("POST", "/nope", body="{}",
                                       headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "not_found")


class BaselineBehaviorTest(HttpTestBase):
    def test_healthz_unchanged(self):
        status, payload = self.request("GET", "/healthz")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "ok")
        self.assertEqual(payload["service"], "siliconrail")
        self.assertIn("version", payload)

    def test_unknown_get_path_404_structure(self):
        status, payload = self.request("GET", "/whatever")
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(payload["error"]["code"], "not_found")
        self.assertIn("no route for /whatever", payload["error"]["message"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

1	"""Unsigned bit-width inference over the parsed circuit IR.
2	
3	The pass re-parses the source with :func:`siliconrail.rtl.parse` (so all
4	lexical, syntactic and semantic failures surface as the same
5	:class:`siliconrail.rtl.RTLParseError` with unchanged ``code``/``line``/
6	``column``/``message``) and then annotates the resulting IR in place:
7	
8	- every expression node inside an assignment target or value gains a
9	  ``width`` field,
10	- every assignment gains ``target_width``, ``value_width`` and
11	  ``conversion`` (one of ``exact``, ``zero_extend``, ``truncate``).
12	
13	Signals are treated as unsigned, matching the current subset. The
14	expression tree itself is never rewritten and constant values are left
15	untouched; ``truncate`` only labels the conversion.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from .rtl import parse
21	
22	# Binary operators whose result is a single bit.
23	_BINARY_ONE_BIT = {"&&", "||", "==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="}
24	# Binary operators whose result takes the left operand's width.
25	_BINARY_LEFT_WIDTH = {"<<", ">>", "<<<", ">>>"}
26	# Unary operators whose result is a single bit (logical not + reductions).
27	_UNARY_ONE_BIT = {"!", "&", "|", "^", "~&", "~|", "~^", "^~"}
28	
29	
30	def _const_width(value: int, declared: int | None) -> int:
31	    if declared is not None:
32	        return declared
33	    # Unsized decimal constants: wide enough to hold the value, at least
34	    # 32 bits; zero is therefore 32 bits as well.
35	    return max(value.bit_length(), 32)
36	
37	
38	def _expr_width(node: dict, declared_widths: dict[str, int]) -> int:
39	    kind = node["kind"]
40	    if kind == "const":
41	        width = _const_width(node["value"], node["width"])
42	    elif kind == "ref":
43	        width = declared_widths[node["name"]]
44	    elif kind == "bit_select":
45	        _expr_width(node["base"], declared_widths)
46	        _expr_width(node["index"], declared_widths)
47	        width = 1
48	    elif kind == "range_select":
49	        _expr_width(node["base"], declared_widths)
50	        width = abs(node["msb"] - node["lsb"]) + 1
51	    elif kind == "concat":
52	        width = sum(_expr_width(item, declared_widths) for item in node["items"])
53	    elif kind == "unary":
54	        operand = _expr_width(node["operand"], declared_widths)
55	        width = 1 if node["op"] in _UNARY_ONE_BIT else operand
56	    elif kind == "binary":
57	        left = _expr_width(node["left"], declared_widths)
58	        right = _expr_width(node["right"], declared_widths)
59	        op = node["op"]
60	        if op in _BINARY_ONE_BIT:
61	            width = 1
62	        elif op in _BINARY_LEFT_WIDTH:
63	            width = left
64	        else:
65	            width = max(left, right)
66	    else:  # pragma: no cover - the parser only emits the kinds above
67	        raise AssertionError(f"unknown expression kind {kind!r}")
68	    node["width"] = width
69	    return width
70	
71	
72	def _conversion(target_width: int, value_width: int) -> str:
73	    if value_width < target_width:
74	        return "zero_extend"
75	    if value_width > target_width:
76	        return "truncate"
77	    return "exact"
78	
79	
80	def analyze(source: str) -> dict:
81	    """Parse ``source`` and annotate the IR with unsigned bit widths."""
82	    ir = parse(source)
83	    for module in ir["modules"]:
84	        declared_widths = {port["name"]: port["width"] for port in module["ports"]}
85	        declared_widths.update({net["name"]: net["width"] for net in module["nets"]})
86	        for assign in module["assigns"]:
87	            target_width = _expr_width(assign["target"], declared_widths)
88	            value_width = _expr_width(assign["value"], declared_widths)
89	            assign["target_width"] = target_width
90	            assign["value_width"] = value_width
91	            assign["conversion"] = _conversion(target_width, value_width)
92	    return ir

1	"""Structural clock-domain-crossing (CDC) analysis over elaborated designs.
2	
3	The checker consumes a design that has already been fully elaborated
4	(hierarchy flattened, parameters evaluated) and therefore describes the
5	circuit as a flat collection of registers, combinational gates and
6	memories connected by nets.  It never rewrites the input design; the
7	optional constraints only steer this one report.
8	
9	Design format (JSON-safe dict)
10	------------------------------
11	- ``top``: optional top-module name (string).
12	- ``elaborated``: optional flag; when explicitly ``false`` the design is
13	  rejected.  A design that still carries ``modules`` (unflattened parse
14	  IR), non-empty ``instances`` or non-empty ``parameters`` is likewise
15	  rejected with :class:`ValueError`.
16	- ``clocks``: list of clock declarations.  ``{"name": "clk"}`` declares a
17	  root clock; ``{"name": "clk_div", "derived_from": "clk", "divide_by": 2}``
18	  declares a clock derived from another declared clock through an
19	  integer divider with a clear phase relation.  Derived clocks share
20	  their root clock's domain relations.
21	- ``ports``: list of ``{"name", "direction", "width"}`` with direction
22	  ``input`` / ``output`` / ``inout`` (``width`` optional, default 1).
23	  Input and inout ports are potential CDC sources in the ``external``
24	  domain.
25	- ``nets``: optional list of ``{"name", "width", "const", "gray_code"}``
26	  giving net widths, constant bindings (non-negative integers) and
27	  gray-code marks.  Constants never produce diagnostics.
28	- ``cells``: list of
29	    - ``{"kind": "dff", "name", "clk", "d", "q", "edge"?, "async_reset"?,
30	      "async_set"?, "width"?, "gray_code"?, "source"?}`` — an edge
31	      triggered register (``edge`` defaults to ``"posedge"``);
32	    - ``{"kind": "logic", "name", "op"?, "inputs": [...], "output"}`` —
33	      a combinational gate;
34	    - ``{"kind": "memory", "name", "write_clock", "write_enable"?,
35	      "write_data"?, "write_addr"?, "read_data"?, "read_addr"?,
36	      "width"?, "source"?}`` — a memory whose write side is clocked by
37	      ``write_clock``.
38	  Every cell may carry ``source`` (e.g. ``{"module", "line", "column"}``)
39	  locating it in the original RTL; the report echoes it as
40	  ``source_info`` / ``dest_info``.
41	
42	Constraints format (optional dict)
43	----------------------------------
44	- ``async_clock_groups``: list of clock-name lists.  Clocks inside one
45	  group are mutually synchronous; clocks in different groups are
46	  asynchronous.
47	- ``synchronous_clocks``: list of clock-name lists whose members are
48	  declared mutually synchronous.  Declaring the same pair synchronous
49	  and asynchronous raises :class:`ValueError`.
50	- ``quasi_static``: list of hierarchical net/cell/port names whose
51	  values are stable at runtime; crossings through them are suppressed.
52	- ``resets``: list of ``{"name", "clock"?}`` (or bare names) declaring
53	  reset nets whose release is handled for the given clock domain (any
54	  domain when ``clock`` is omitted); recognized reset-release crossings
55	  are reported as information instead of errors.
56	
57	Constraint entries referencing objects that do not exist in the design
58	raise :class:`KeyError`.
59	
60	Report format
61	-------------
62	``{"top", "domains", "clock_relations", "diagnostics", "summary"}`` —
63	all JSON-serializable and deterministic.  ``diagnostics`` is sorted by
64	``(source, dest)`` hierarchical paths and carries ``source_domain``,
65	``dest_domain``, ``source``, ``dest``, ``width``, ``category``,
66	``severity`` (``error`` / ``warning`` / ``info``), ``message`` and the
67	RTL ``source_info`` / ``dest_info`` when available.  Categories:
68	``synchronized``, ``gray_code``, ``multi_bit_coherence``,
69	``combinational``, ``state_element``, ``memory_write_control``,
70	``async_reset_release`` and ``sync_chain_fanout``.
71	"""
72	
73	from __future__ import annotations
74	
75	_SEVERITY_RANK = {"info": 1, "warning": 2, "error": 3}
76	_EDGES = ("posedge", "negedge")
77	_DIRECTIONS = ("input", "output", "inout")
78	_EXTERNAL = "external"
79	
80	
81	def check(design: dict, constraints: dict | None = None) -> dict:
82	    """Run structural CDC analysis over an elaborated design.
83	
84	    Raises ``TypeError`` when ``design`` is not a dict (or ``constraints``
85	    is neither a dict nor ``None``), :class:`ValueError` when the design
86	    is not fully elaborated, a clock connection cannot be resolved, or
87	    the constraints are self-contradictory, and :class:`KeyError` when a
88	    constraint references an object that does not exist in the design.
89	    Unsafe crossings are reported in the returned report, never raised.
90	    """
91	    if not isinstance(design, dict):
92	        raise TypeError(f"design must be a dict, got {type(design).__name__}")
93	    if constraints is not None and not isinstance(constraints, dict):
94	        raise TypeError(
95	            f"constraints must be a dict or None, got {type(constraints).__name__}"
96	        )
97	    model = _Model(design)
98	    ctx = _Context(model, constraints or {})
99	    return _analyze(model, ctx)

102	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
103	# Validation helpers
104	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	
106	
107	def _positive_int(value) -> bool:
108	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 1
109	
110	
111	def _width_of(entry: dict, what: str) -> int:
112	    width = entry.get("width", 1)
113	    if not _positive_int(width):
114	        raise ValueError(f"{what}: 'width' must be a positive integer")
115	    return width
116	
117	
118	def _name_of(entry: dict, what: str) -> str:
119	    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
120	        raise ValueError(f"each {what} must be an object")
121	    name = entry.get("name")
122	    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
123	        raise ValueError(f"each {what} requires a non-empty string 'name'")
124	    return name
125	
126	
127	def _required_net(entry: dict, key: str, name: str) -> str:
128	    value = entry.get(key)
129	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
130	        raise ValueError(f"cell {name!r} requires a string {key!r}")
131	    return value
132	
133	
134	def _optional_net(entry: dict, key: str, name: str) -> str | None:
135	    value = entry.get(key)
136	    if value is None:
137	        return None
138	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
139	        raise ValueError(f"cell {name!r}: {key!r} must be a non-empty string")
140	    return value
141	
142	
143	def _list_of(entries, key: str) -> list:
144	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
145	        raise ValueError(f"{key!r} must be a list")
146	    return entries
147	
148	
149	def _pairs(names) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
150	    ordered = sorted(set(names))
151	    return [
152	        (ordered[i], ordered[j])
153	        for i in range(len(ordered))
154	        for j in range(i + 1, len(ordered))
155	    ]

162	
163	class _Model:
164	    """Validated, indexed view of the elaborated design (read-only)."""
165	
166	    def __init__(self, design: dict) -> None:
167	        if (
168	            design.get("elaborated") is False
169	            or design.get("modules")
170	            or design.get("instances")
171	            or design.get("parameters")
172	        ):
173	            raise ValueError(
174	                "design is not fully elaborated: hierarchy and parameters "
175	                "must be resolved before CDC analysis"
176	            )
177	        self.top = design.get("top")
178	        if self.top is not None and not isinstance(self.top, str):
179	            raise ValueError("'top' must be a string")
180	
181	        self.clocks: dict[str, dict] = {}
182	        self._parse_clocks(_list_of(design.get("clocks", []), "clocks"))
183	
184	        self.ports: dict[str, dict] = {}
185	        self.net_width: dict[str, int] = {}
186	        self.net_const: dict[str, int] = {}
187	        self.gray_nets: set[str] = set()
188	        self.all_nets: set[str] = set()
189	        self.net_driver: dict[str, tuple] = {}
190	        self.net_loads: dict[str, list] = {}
191	        self._parse_nets(_list_of(design.get("nets", []), "nets"))
192	        self._parse_ports(_list_of(design.get("ports", []), "ports"))
193	
194	        self.cells: dict[str, dict] = {}
195	        self._parse_cells(_list_of(design.get("cells", []), "cells"))
196	
197	        self.ff_domain: dict[str, str] = {}
198	        self.domain_clock: dict[str, str] = {}
199	        self.domain_edge: dict[str, str] = {}
200	        self._resolve_domains()
201	
202	    # -- clocks ------------------------------------------------------------
203	
204	    def _parse_clocks(self, entries: list) -> None:
205	        raw: dict[str, dict] = {}
206	        for entry in entries:
207	            name = _name_of(entry, "clock")
208	            if name in raw:
209	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate clock {name!r}")
210	            raw[name] = entry
211	        for name in raw:
212	            self._resolve_clock(name, raw, ())
213	
214	    def _resolve_clock(self, name: str, raw: dict, stack: tuple) -> None:
215	        if name in self.clocks:
216	            return
217	        if name in stack:
218	            raise ValueError(f"clock derivation cycle involving {name!r}")
219	        entry = raw[name]
220	        parent = entry.get("derived_from")
221	        if parent is None:
222	            divide = entry.get("divide_by", 1)
223	            if not _positive_int(divide) or divide != 1:
224	                raise ValueError(f"root clock {name!r} cannot have 'divide_by'")
225	            self.clocks[name] = {"root": name, "divide_by": 1}
226	            return
227	        if parent not in raw:
228	            raise ValueError(f"clock {name!r} derives from unknown clock {parent!r}")
229	        divide = entry.get("divide_by")
230	        if not _positive_int(divide):
231	            raise ValueError(
232	                f"derived clock {name!r} requires a positive integer 'divide_by'"
233	            )
234	        self._resolve_clock(parent, raw, stack + (name,))
235	        base = self.clocks[parent]
236	        self.clocks[name] = {
237	            "root": base["root"],
238	            "divide_by": base["divide_by"] * divide,
239	        }
240	
241	    # -- nets and ports ------------------------------------------------------
242	
243	    def _parse_nets(self, entries: list) -> None:
244	        for entry in entries:
245	            name = _name_of(entry, "net")
246	            if name in self.all_nets:
247	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate net {name!r}")
248	            self.net_width[name] = _width_of(entry, f"net {name!r}")
249	            const = entry.get("const")
250	            if const is not None:
251	                if not isinstance(const, int) or isinstance(const, bool) or const < 0:
252	                    raise ValueError(f"net {name!r}: 'const' must be a non-negative integer")
253	                self.net_const[name] = const
254	            if entry.get("gray_code"):
255	                self.gray_nets.add(name)
256	            self.all_nets.add(name)
257	
258	    def _parse_ports(self, entries: list) -> None:
259	        for entry in entries:
260	            name = _name_of(entry, "port")
261	            direction = entry.get("direction", "input")
262	            if direction not in _DIRECTIONS:
263	                raise ValueError(
264	                    f"port {name!r}: 'direction' must be one of {_DIRECTIONS}"
265	                )
266	            if name in self.net_const:
267	                raise ValueError(f"port {name!r} conflicts with a constant net")
268	            if name in self.all_nets:
269	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate port {name!r}")
270	            width = _width_of(entry, f"port {name!r}")
271	            self.ports[name] = {"direction": direction, "width": width}
272	            self.net_width.setdefault(name, width)
273	            self.all_nets.add(name)
274	            if direction in ("input", "inout"):
275	                self.net_driver[name] = ("port", name)
276	
277	    # -- cells ---------------------------------------------------------------
278	
279	    def _add_driver(self, net: str, owner: tuple) -> None:
280	        if net in self.net_const:
281	            raise ValueError(f"net {net!r} is both constant and driven")
282	        if net in self.net_driver:
283	            raise ValueError(f"net {net!r} has multiple drivers")
284	        self.net_driver[net] = owner
285	        self.all_nets.add(net)
286	
287	    def _add_load(self, net: str, load: tuple) -> None:
288	        self.net_loads.setdefault(net, []).append(load)
289	        self.all_nets.add(net)
290	
291	    def _parse_cells(self, entries: list) -> None:
292	        for entry in entries:
293	            name = _name_of(entry, "cell")
294	            if name in self.cells:
295	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate cell {name!r}")
296	            kind = entry.get("kind")
297	            if kind == "dff":
298	                cell = self._dff(entry)
299	            elif kind == "logic":
300	                cell = self._logic(entry)
301	            elif kind == "memory":
302	                cell = self._memory(entry)
303	            else:
304	                raise ValueError(f"unsupported cell kind {kind!r}")
305	            self.cells[name] = cell
306	
307	    def _dff(self, entry: dict) -> dict:
308	        name = entry["name"]
309	        edge = entry.get("edge", "posedge")
310	        if edge not in _EDGES:
311	            raise ValueError(
312	                f"register {name!r}: 'edge' must be one of {_EDGES}"
313	            )
314	        cell = {
315	            "kind": "dff",
316	            "name": name,
317	            "clk": _required_net(entry, "clk", name),
318	            "d": _required_net(entry, "d", name),
319	            "q": _required_net(entry, "q", name),
320	            "edge": edge,
321	            "async_reset": _optional_net(entry, "async_reset", name),
322	            "async_set": _optional_net(entry, "async_set", name),
323	            "width": _width_of(entry, f"register {name!r}"),
324	            "gray": bool(entry.get("gray_code")),
325	            "source": entry.get("source"),
326	        }
327	        self._add_driver(cell["q"], ("dff", name))
328	        self.net_width.setdefault(cell["q"], cell["width"])
329	        self._add_load(cell["clk"], ("dff", name, "clk"))
330	        self._add_load(cell["d"], ("dff", name, "d"))
331	        if cell["async_reset"]:
332	            self._add_load(cell["async_reset"], ("dff", name, "async_reset"))
333	        if cell["async_set"]:
334	            self._add_load(cell["async_set"], ("dff", name, "async_set"))
335	        return cell
336	
337	    def _logic(self, entry: dict) -> dict:
338	        name = entry["name"]
339	        inputs = entry.get("inputs", [])
340	        if not isinstance(inputs, list) or any(not isinstance(i, str) for i in inputs):
341	            raise ValueError(f"logic cell {name!r}: 'inputs' must be a list of nets")
342	        cell = {
343	            "kind": "logic",
344	            "name": name,
345	            "op": entry.get("op", "buf"),
346	            "inputs": list(inputs),
347	            "output": _required_net(entry, "output", name),
348	            "source": entry.get("source"),
349	        }
350	        self._add_driver(cell["output"], ("logic", name))
351	        for net in cell["inputs"]:
352	            self._add_load(net, ("logic", name, "input"))
353	        return cell
354	
355	    def _memory(self, entry: dict) -> dict:
356	        name = entry["name"]
357	        cell = {"kind": "memory", "name": name, "source": entry.get("source")}
358	        for pin in (
359	            "write_clock",
360	            "write_enable",
361	            "write_data",
362	            "write_addr",
363	            "read_data",
364	            "read_addr",
365	        ):
366	            cell[pin] = _optional_net(entry, pin, name)
367	        if cell["write_clock"] is None:
368	            raise ValueError(f"memory {name!r} requires a 'write_clock' net")
369	        cell["width"] = _width_of(entry, f"memory {name!r}")
370	        if cell["read_data"]:
371	            self._add_driver(cell["read_data"], ("memory", name))
372	            self.net_width.setdefault(cell["read_data"], cell["width"])
373	        for pin in ("write_clock", "write_enable", "write_data", "write_addr", "read_addr"):
374	            if cell[pin]:
375	                self._add_load(cell[pin], ("memory", name, pin))
376	        return cell
377	
378	    # -- clock domains ---------------------------------------------------------
379	
380	    def _clock_for_net(self, net: str, user: str) -> str:
381	        if net in self.clocks:
382	            return net
383	        if net in self.net_const:
384	            raise ValueError(
385	                f"clock connection {net!r} of {user!r} cannot be resolved to a clock"
386	            )
387	        driver = self.net_driver.get(net)
388	        if driver is not None and driver[0] != "port":
389	            raise ValueError(
390	                f"clock connection {net!r} of {user!r} cannot be resolved to a clock"
391	            )
392	        # An undriven net or a primary input used as a clock is an
393	        # implicit root clock of the design.
394	        self.clocks[net] = {"root": net, "divide_by": 1}
395	        return net
396	
397	    def _resolve_domains(self) -> None:
398	        for cell in self.cells.values():
399	            if cell["kind"] == "dff":
400	                clock = self._clock_for_net(cell["clk"], cell["name"])
401	                domain = clock if cell["edge"] == "posedge" else f"{clock}@{cell['edge']}"
402	                self.ff_domain[cell["name"]] = domain
403	                self.domain_clock[domain] = clock
404	                self.domain_edge[domain] = cell["edge"]
405	            elif cell["kind"] == "memory":
406	                clock = self._clock_for_net(cell["write_clock"], cell["name"])
407	                self.ff_domain[cell["name"]] = clock
408	                self.domain_clock.setdefault(clock, clock)
409	                self.domain_edge.setdefault(clock, "posedge")
410

414	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
415	
416	
417	def _cell_outputs(cell: dict) -> list[str]:
418	    if cell["kind"] == "dff":
419	        return [cell["q"]]
420	    if cell["kind"] == "logic":
421	        return [cell["output"]]
422	    return [cell["read_data"]] if cell.get("read_data") else []

424	
425	class _Context:
426	    """Validated constraints plus the clock-relation oracle."""
427	
428	    def __init__(self, model: _Model, constraints: dict) -> None:
429	        self.declared_sync, self.declared_async = self._clock_groups(model, constraints)
430	        self.quasi_nets = self._quasi_static(model, constraints.get("quasi_static", []))
431	        self.reset_nets = self._resets(model, constraints.get("resets", []))
432	
433	    @staticmethod
434	    def _group_list(constraints: dict, key: str) -> list[list[str]]:
435	        groups = constraints.get(key, [])
436	        if not isinstance(groups, list):
437	            raise ValueError(f"{key!r} must be a list of clock-name lists")
438	        result = []
439	        for group in groups:
440	            if not isinstance(group, list) or any(
441	                not isinstance(c, str) for c in group
442	            ):
443	                raise ValueError(f"{key!r} must be a list of clock-name lists")
444	            result.append(sorted(set(group)))
445	        return result
446	
447	    def _clock_groups(self, model: _Model, constraints: dict):
448	        async_groups = self._group_list(constraints, "async_clock_groups")
449	        sync_groups = self._group_list(constraints, "synchronous_clocks")
450	        for group in async_groups + sync_groups:
451	            for clock in group:
452	                if clock not in model.clocks:
453	                    raise KeyError(f"constraint references unknown clock {clock!r}")
454	        seen: dict[str, int] = {}
455	        for index, group in enumerate(async_groups):
456	            for clock in group:
457	                if clock in seen:
458	                    raise ValueError(
459	                        f"clock {clock!r} appears in multiple asynchronous clock groups"
460	                    )
461	                seen[clock] = index
462	        sync_pairs = set()
463	        for group in async_groups + sync_groups:
464	            sync_pairs.update(_pairs(group))
465	        async_pairs = set()
466	        for i in range(len(async_groups)):
467	            for j in range(i + 1, len(async_groups)):
468	                for a in async_groups[i]:
469	                    for b in async_groups[j]:
470	                        async_pairs.add((min(a, b), max(a, b)))
471	        both = sync_pairs & async_pairs
472	        if both:
473	            a, b = sorted(both)[0]
474	            raise ValueError(
475	                f"clock pair {a!r} / {b!r} is declared both synchronous and asynchronous"
476	            )
477	        return sync_pairs, async_pairs
478	
479	    @staticmethod
480	    def _resolve_objects(model: _Model, name: str) -> list[str]:
481	        if name in model.cells:
482	            return _cell_outputs(model.cells[name])
483	        if name in model.all_nets:
484	            return [name]
485	        raise KeyError(f"constraint references unknown object {name!r}")
486	
487	    def _quasi_static(self, model: _Model, names) -> set[str]:
488	        if not isinstance(names, list):
489	            raise ValueError("'quasi_static' must be a list of names")
490	        nets: set[str] = set()
491	        for name in names:
492	            if not isinstance(name, str):
493	                raise ValueError("'quasi_static' entries must be strings")
494	            nets.update(self._resolve_objects(model, name))
495	        return nets
496	
497	    def _resets(self, model: _Model, entries) -> dict:
498	        if not isinstance(entries, list):
499	            raise ValueError("'resets' must be a list")
500	        resets: dict[str, set | None] = {}
501	        for entry in entries:
502	            if isinstance(entry, str):
503	                name, clock = entry, None
504	            elif isinstance(entry, dict):
505	                name = entry.get("name")
506	                clock = entry.get("clock")
507	                if not isinstance(name, str):
508	                    raise ValueError("reset entries require a string 'name'")
509	            else:
510	                raise ValueError("reset entries must be strings or objects")
511	            targets = self._resolve_objects(model, name)
512	            if clock is not None and clock not in model.clocks:
513	                raise KeyError(f"constraint references unknown clock {clock!r}")
514	            for net in targets:
515	                if clock is None:
516	                    resets[net] = None  # recognized in every domain
517	                elif net not in resets:
518	                    resets[net] = {clock}
519	                elif resets[net] is not None:
520	                    resets[net].add(clock)
521	        return resets
522	
523	    # -- relations -----------------------------------------------------------
524	
525	    def relation(self, model: _Model, clock_a: str, clock_b: str) -> str:
526	        if clock_a == clock_b:
527	            return "synchronous"
528	        pair = (min(clock_a, clock_b), max(clock_a, clock_b))
529	        if pair in self.declared_async:
530	            return "asynchronous"
531	        if pair in self.declared_sync:
532	            return "synchronous"
533	        if model.clocks[clock_a]["root"] == model.clocks[clock_b]["root"]:
534	            # Same root clock, recognizable integer division, clear phase.
535	            return "synchronous"
536	        return "potentially_asynchronous"
537	
538	    def compatible(self, model: _Model, domain_a: str, domain_b: str) -> bool:
539	        if domain_a == domain_b:
540	            return True
541	        if domain_a == _EXTERNAL or domain_b == _EXTERNAL:
542	            return False
543	        relation = self.relation(
544	            model, model.domain_clock[domain_a], model.domain_clock[domain_b]
545	        )
546	        return relation == "synchronous"
547

554	def _sources(model: _Model, ctx: _Context) -> list[dict]:
555	    sources = []
556	    for name, cell in model.cells.items():
557	        if cell["kind"] == "dff":
558	            sources.append(
559	                {
560	                    "net": cell["q"],
561	                    "domain": model.ff_domain[name],
562	                    "name": name,
563	                    "info": cell["source"],
564	                    "gray": cell["gray"] or cell["q"] in model.gray_nets,
565	                    "width": model.net_width.get(cell["q"], cell["width"]),
566	                }
567	            )
568	        elif cell["kind"] == "memory" and cell["read_data"]:
569	            sources.append(
570	                {
571	                    "net": cell["read_data"],
572	                    "domain": model.ff_domain[name],
573	                    "name": name,
574	                    "info": cell["source"],
575	                    "gray": cell["read_data"] in model.gray_nets,
576	                    "width": model.net_width.get(cell["read_data"], cell["width"]),
577	                }
578	            )
579	    for port_name, port in model.ports.items():
580	        if port["direction"] in ("input", "inout"):
581	            sources.append(
582	                {
583	                    "net": port_name,
584	                    "domain": _EXTERNAL,
585	                    "name": port_name,
586	                    "info": None,
587	                    "gray": port_name in model.gray_nets,
588	                    "width": port["width"],
589	                }
590	            )
591	    sources.sort(key=lambda s: s["name"])
592	    return [
593	        s
594	        for s in sources
595	        if s["net"] not in ctx.quasi_nets and s["net"] not in model.net_const
596	    ]

598	
599	def _chain(model: _Model, first: str, domain: str) -> tuple[int, bool]:
600	    """Length of the register chain starting at ``first`` and whether the
601	    first stage fans out to anything besides the next chain stage."""
602	    length = 1
603	    fanout = False
604	    seen = {first}
605	    current = first
606	    is_first = True
607	    while True:
608	        loads = model.net_loads.get(model.cells[current]["q"], [])
609	        if is_first and len(loads) > 1:
610	            fanout = True
611	        followers = sorted(
612	            cell_name
613	            for kind, cell_name, pin in loads
614	            if kind == "dff"
615	            and pin == "d"
616	            and model.ff_domain.get(cell_name) == domain
617	            and cell_name not in seen
618	        )
619	        if not followers:
620	            return length, fanout
621	        current = followers[0]
622	        seen.add(current)
623	        length += 1
624	        is_first = False
625	
626	
627	def _message(category: str, source: dict, dest: str, dest_domain: str, stages: int) -> str:
628	    src_domain = source["domain"]
629	    if category == "synchronized":
630	        return (
631	            f"single-bit crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain "
632	            f"{dest_domain!r} is synchronized by a {stages}-stage register chain"
633	        )
634	    if category == "sync_chain_fanout":
635	        return (
636	            f"synchronizer first stage {dest!r} fans out to logic other than "
637	            f"the next synchronizer stage; crossing from domain {src_domain!r} "
638	            f"to domain {dest_domain!r} is unsafe"
639	        )
640	    if category == "state_element":
641	        return (
642	            f"crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain {dest_domain!r} is "
643	            f"captured by {dest!r} without synchronization"
644	        )
645	    if category == "combinational":
646	        return (
647	            f"crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain {dest_domain!r} "
648	            f"passes through combinational logic before capture by {dest!r}"
649	        )
650	    if category == "multi_bit_coherence":
651	        return (
652	            f"multi-bit crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain "
653	            f"{dest_domain!r} is synchronized per bit at {dest!r} but bit "
654	            f"coherence is not guaranteed"
655	        )
656	    if category == "gray_code":
657	        return (
658	            f"multi-bit crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain "
659	            f"{dest_domain!r} at {dest!r} uses gray-code transfer "
660	            f"(adjacent values differ by one bit)"
661	        )
662	    if category == "memory_write_control":
663	        return (
664	            f"crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain {dest_domain!r} "
665	            f"drives write control of memory {dest!r}"
666	        )
667	    if category == "async_reset_release":
668	        return (
669	            f"crossing from domain {src_domain!r} to domain {dest_domain!r} "
670	            f"drives the asynchronous reset/set of {dest!r}"
671	        )
672	    raise AssertionError(f"unknown category {category!r}")  # pragma: no cover
673	
674	
675	def _diag(
676	    model: _Model,
677	    source: dict,
678	    dest_cell: dict,
679	    dest_domain: str,
680	    category: str,
681	    severity: str,
682	    stages: int = 0,
683	) -> dict:
684	    return {
685	        "source_domain": source["domain"],
686	        "dest_domain": dest_domain,
687	        "source": source["name"],
688	        "dest": dest_cell["name"],
689	        "width": source["width"],
690	        "category": category,
691	        "severity": severity,
692	        "message": _message(category, source, dest_cell["name"], dest_domain, stages),
693	        "source_info": source["info"],
694	        "dest_info": dest_cell.get("source"),
695	    }
696	
697	
698	def _capture_diag(
699	    model: _Model, source: dict, dest_cell: dict, via_logic: bool
700	) -> dict:
701	    dest_domain = model.ff_domain[dest_cell["name"]]
702	    if via_logic:
703	        return _diag(model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "combinational", "error")
704	    stages, fanout = _chain(model, dest_cell["name"], dest_domain)
705	    if source["width"] == 1:
706	        if stages >= 2:
707	            if fanout:
708	                return _diag(
709	                    model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain,
710	                    "sync_chain_fanout", "error", stages,
711	                )
712	            return _diag(
713	                model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "synchronized", "info", stages
714	            )
715	        return _diag(model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "state_element", "error")
716	    if stages >= 2:
717	        if source["gray"]:
718	            return _diag(
719	                model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "gray_code", "info", stages
720	            )
721	        return _diag(
722	            model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain,
723	            "multi_bit_coherence", "warning", stages,
724	        )
725	    return _diag(model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "state_element", "error")
726	
727	
728	def _reset_diag(model: _Model, ctx: _Context, source: dict, dest_cell: dict) -> dict:
729	    dest_domain = model.ff_domain[dest_cell["name"]]
730	    severity = "error"
731	    if source["net"] in ctx.reset_nets:
732	        clocks = ctx.reset_nets[source["net"]]
733	        if clocks is None or model.domain_clock[dest_domain] in clocks:
734	            severity = "info"
735	    return _diag(
736	        model, source, dest_cell, dest_domain, "async_reset_release", severity
737	    )
738	
739	
740	def _trace(model: _Model, ctx: _Context, source: dict) -> list[dict]:
741	    results = []
742	    seen: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
743	    stack = [(source["net"], False)]
744	    while stack:
745	        net, via_logic = stack.pop()
746	        if (net, via_logic) in seen:
747	            continue
748	        seen.add((net, via_logic))
749	        if net in ctx.quasi_nets or net in model.net_const:
750	            continue
751	        for kind, cell_name, pin in model.net_loads.get(net, ()):
752	            cell = model.cells[cell_name]
753	            if kind == "logic":
754	                stack.append((cell["output"], True))
755	            elif kind == "dff":
756	                if pin == "clk":
757	                    continue  # clock pins are not data sinks
758	                dest_domain = model.ff_domain[cell_name]
759	                if ctx.compatible(model, source["domain"], dest_domain):
760	                    continue
761	                if pin == "d":
762	                    results.append(_capture_diag(model, source, cell, via_logic))
763	                else:  # async_reset / async_set
764	                    results.append(_reset_diag(model, ctx, source, cell))
765	            elif kind == "memory":
766	                if pin == "write_clock":
767	                    continue
768	                if pin == "read_addr":
769	                    if cell["read_data"]:
770	                        stack.append((cell["read_data"], True))
771	                    continue
772	                dest_domain = model.ff_domain[cell_name]
773	                if ctx.compatible(model, source["domain"], dest_domain):
774	                    continue
775	                if pin == "write_enable":
776	                    results.append(
777	                        _diag(
778	                            model, source, cell, dest_domain,
779	                            "memory_write_control", "error",
780	                        )
781	                    )
782	                else:  # write_data / write_addr
783	                    results.append(
784	                        _diag(
785	                            model, source, cell, dest_domain,
786	                            "state_element", "error",
787	                        )
788	                    )
789	    return results
790	
791	
792	def _outranks(candidate: dict, current: dict) -> bool:
793	    cand = _SEVERITY_RANK[candidate["severity"]]
794	    cur = _SEVERITY_RANK[current["severity"]]
795	    if cand != cur:
796	        return cand > cur
797	    return candidate["category"] < current["category"]
798	
799	
800	def _analyze(model: _Model, ctx: _Context) -> dict:
801	    diagnostics: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
802	    for source in _sources(model, ctx):
803	        for diag in _trace(model, ctx, source):
804	            key = (diag["source"], diag["dest"])
805	            previous = diagnostics.get(key)
806	            if previous is None or _outranks(diag, previous):
807	                diagnostics[key] = diag
808	    ordered = sorted(diagnostics.values(), key=lambda d: (d["source"], d["dest"]))
809	
810	    summary = {"total": len(ordered), "error": 0, "warning": 0, "info": 0}
811	    for diag in ordered:
812	        summary[diag["severity"]] += 1
813	
814	    domains = [
815	        {
816	            "name": name,
817	            "clock": model.domain_clock[name],
818	            "edge": model.domain_edge[name],
819	            "root": model.clocks[model.domain_clock[name]]["root"],
820	            "divide_by": model.clocks[model.domain_clock[name]]["divide_by"],
821	        }
822	        for name in sorted(set(model.ff_domain.values()))
823	    ]
824	    relations = [
825	        {"clock_a": a, "clock_b": b, "relation": ctx.relation(model, a, b)}
826	        for a, b in _pairs(model.clocks)
827	    ]
828	    return {
829	        "top": model.top,
830	        "domains": domains,
831	        "clock_relations": relations,
832	        "diagnostics": ordered,
833	        "summary": summary,
834	    }

"""Core service surface for SiliconRail.

Exposes process health reporting and the Verilog RTL parser. Keep the
public surface here backward compatible; later capabilities described in
README.md plug in behind this module.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from . import __version__
from .cdc import check as _check_cdc
from .rtl import RTLParseError, parse
from .widths import analyze as _analyze_widths


class Service:
    """SiliconRail service: health reporting and RTL parsing."""

    name = "siliconrail"
    version = __version__

    def health(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok", "service": self.name, "version": self.version}

    def parse_rtl(self, source: str) -> dict:
        """Parse Verilog-2001 combinational subset into a JSON-safe circuit IR.

        Raises ``TypeError`` when ``source`` is not a string and
        :class:`RTLParseError` for any lexical, syntactic or semantic
        failure (an empty string is a syntax error).
        """
        if not isinstance(source, str):
            raise TypeError(f"source must be str, got {type(source).__name__}")
        return parse(source)

    def analyze_widths(self, source: str) -> dict:
        """Parse like :meth:`parse_rtl` and annotate the IR with bit widths.

        Every expression node in an assignment target or value gains a
        ``width`` field; every assignment gains ``target_width``,
        ``value_width`` and ``conversion`` (``exact``, ``zero_extend`` or
        ``truncate``). Raises ``TypeError`` when ``source`` is not a string
        and :class:`RTLParseError` for any parse failure, exactly like
        :meth:`parse_rtl`.
        """
        if not isinstance(source, str):
            raise TypeError(f"source must be str, got {type(source).__name__}")
        return _analyze_widths(source)

    def check_cdc(self, design: dict, constraints: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        """Run structural clock-domain-crossing analysis on an elaborated design.

        ``design`` is a flat, fully elaborated netlist (registers,
        combinational gates and memories connected by nets; see
        :mod:`siliconrail.cdc` for the format). ``constraints`` may
        declare asynchronous clock groups, synchronous clock groups,
        quasi-static objects and reset definitions; constraints only
        steer this report and never modify the design.

        Returns a JSON-serializable deterministic report. Raises
        ``TypeError`` when ``design`` is not a dict, ``ValueError`` when
        the design is not fully elaborated, a clock connection cannot be
        resolved, or the constraints are contradictory, and ``KeyError``
        when a constraint references an object absent from the design.
        Unsafe crossings are analysis results, not failures.
        """
        return _check_cdc(design, constraints)


__all__ = ["Service", "RTLParseError"]

3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import json
7	import os
8	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
9	
10	from .rtl import RTLParseError
11	from .service import Service
12	
13	
14	def env_address() -> tuple[str, int]:
15	    raw = os.environ.get("SILICONRAIL_ADDR", "127.0.0.1:8080")
16	    host, _, port = raw.rpartition(":")
17	    if not host or not port.isdigit():
18	        raise SystemExit(f"invalid SILICONRAIL_ADDR: {raw!r}")
19	    return host, int(port)
20	
21	
22	_INVALID_REQUEST_MESSAGE = "body must be a JSON object with a string 'source'"
23	
24	
25	class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
26	    service = Service()
27	
28	    def send_json(self, status: int, payload: dict) -> None:
29	        body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
30	        self.send_response(status)
31	        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
32	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
33	        self.end_headers()
34	        self.wfile.write(body)
35	
36	    def do_GET(self) -> None:
37	        if self.path == "/healthz":
38	            self.send_json(200, self.service.health())
39	            return
40	        self.send_json(404, {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": f"no route for {self.path}"}})
41	
42	    _POST_ROUTES = {
43	        "/v1/rtl/parse": "parse_rtl",
44	        "/v1/rtl/widths": "analyze_widths",
45	    }
46	
47	    def do_POST(self) -> None:
48	        if self.path == "/v1/cdc/check":
49	            self.do_cdc_check()
50	            return
51	        method_name = self._POST_ROUTES.get(self.path)
52	        if method_name is None:
53	            self.send_json(404, {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": f"no route for {self.path}"}})
54	            return
55	        try:
56	            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
57	        except ValueError:
58	            length = 0
59	        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length > 0 else b""
60	        try:
61	            payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
62	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
63	            self.invalid_request()
64	            return
65	        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("source"), str):
66	            self.invalid_request()
67	            return
68	        try:
69	            ir = getattr(self.service, method_name)(payload["source"])
70	        except RTLParseError as exc:
71	            self.send_json(
72	                422,
73	                {
74	                    "error": {
75	                        "code": exc.code,
76	                        "line": exc.line,
77	                        "column": exc.column,
78	                        "message": exc.message,
79	                    }
80	                },
81	            )
82	            return
83	        self.send_json(200, ir)
84	
85	    def do_cdc_check(self) -> None:
86	        try:
87	            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
88	        except ValueError:
89	            length = 0
90	        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length > 0 else b""
91	        try:
92	            payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
93	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
94	            payload = None
95	        constraints = payload.get("constraints") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
96	        if (
97	            not isinstance(payload, dict)
98	            or not isinstance(payload.get("design"), dict)
99	            or (constraints is not None and not isinstance(constraints, dict))
100	        ):
101	            self.send_json(
102	                400,
103	                {
104	                    "error": {
105	                        "code": "invalid_request",
106	                        "message": "body must be a JSON object with an object 'design'"
107	                        " and an optional object 'constraints'",
108	                    }
109	                },
110	            )
111	            return
112	        try:
113	            report = self.service.check_cdc(payload["design"], constraints)
114	        except ValueError as exc:
115	            self.send_json(
116	                422, {"error": {"code": "invalid_design", "message": str(exc)}}
117	            )
118	            return
119	        except KeyError as exc:
120	            message = exc.args[0] if exc.args else str(exc)
121	            self.send_json(
122	                422, {"error": {"code": "unknown_object", "message": message}}
123	            )
124	            return
125	        self.send_json(200, report)
126	
127	    def invalid_request(self) -> None:
128	        self.send_json(
129	            400,
130	            {"error": {"code": "invalid_request", "message": _INVALID_REQUEST_MESSAGE}},
131	        )
132	
133	    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: object) -> None:
134	        """Silence per-request logging so recorded output stays stable."""
135	
136	
137	def main() -> int:
138	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="siliconrail.server", description="芯片前端设计与 RTL 流程工具链")
139	    host, port = env_address()
140	    parser.add_argument("--host", default=host)
141	    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=port)
142	    args = parser.parse_args()
143	    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((args.host, args.port), Handler)
144	    print(f"SiliconRail listening on http://{args.host}:{httpd.server_address[1]}", flush=True)
145	    try:
146	        httpd.serve_forever()
147	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
148	        pass
149	    finally:
150	        httpd.server_close()
151	    return 0
152	
153	
154	if __name__ == "__main__":
155	    raise SystemExit(main())

import copy
import json
import unittest

from siliconrail.service import Service


def dff(name, clk, d, q, **kw):
    cell = {"kind": "dff", "name": name, "clk": clk, "d": d, "q": q}
    cell.update(kw)
    return cell


def logic(name, inputs, output, op="buf"):
    return {"kind": "logic", "name": name, "op": op, "inputs": inputs, "output": output}


def design(cells=(), clocks=(), ports=(), nets=(), top="top", **extra):
    result = {
        "top": top,
        "elaborated": True,
        "clocks": list(clocks),
        "ports": list(ports),
        "nets": list(nets),
        "cells": list(cells),
    }
    result.update(extra)
    return result


def two_clock_crossing(dest_cells, extra_cells=(), **kw):
    """Source register in clk_a feeding whatever ``dest_cells`` need."""
    cells = [
        dff("u_tx/req", "clk_a", "u_tx/req_d", "u_tx/req_q",
            source={"module": "tx", "line": 3, "column": 2}),
        *extra_cells,
        *dest_cells,
    ]
    return design(
        cells,
        clocks=[{"name": "clk_a"}, {"name": "clk_b"}],
        **kw,
    )


class CdcDirectTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.service = Service()

    def check(self, design_dict, constraints=None):
        return self.service.check_cdc(design_dict, constraints)

    # -- trivial designs -----------------------------------------------------

    def test_empty_design_returns_zero_diagnostics(self):
        for empty in ({"elaborated": True}, design()):
            report = self.check(empty)
            self.assertEqual(report["diagnostics"], [])
            self.assertEqual(
                report["summary"], {"total": 0, "error": 0, "warning": 0, "info": 0}
            )
            self.assertEqual(report["domains"], [])
            self.assertEqual(report["clock_relations"], [])
            json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True)

    def test_pure_combinational_design_returns_zero_diagnostics(self):
        report = self.check(
            design(
                cells=[logic("g0", ["a"], "n0"), logic("g1", ["n0"], "o")],
                ports=[
                    {"name": "a", "direction": "input"},
                    {"name": "o", "direction": "output"},
                ],
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(report["diagnostics"], [])
        self.assertEqual(report["summary"]["total"], 0)

    def test_same_domain_paths_produce_no_diagnostics(self):
        report = self.check(
            design(
                cells=[
                    dff("r1", "clk", "d1", "q1"),
                    logic("g", ["q1"], "n"),
                    dff("r2", "clk", "n", "q2"),
                ],
                clocks=[{"name": "clk"}],
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(report["diagnostics"], [])

    def test_same_clock_opposite_edges_are_synchronous(self):
        report = self.check(
            design(
                cells=[
                    dff("r1", "clk", "d1", "q1"),
                    dff("r2", "clk", "q1", "q2", edge="negedge"),
                ],
                clocks=[{"name": "clk"}],
            )
        )
        self.assertEqual(report["diagnostics"], [])

    def test_constant_nets_produce_no_diagnostics(self):

        self.assertEqual(len(report["diagnostics"]), 1)
